reason: REAL, and it survived every attack I could bring. Driven in Playwright on ?v=paper and ?v=ink at 1440x960 and 390x844, typing titles into #b-edit-title (which carries no maxlength) and pressing .b-step[data-delta="7"], then reading .b-undoText. (a) The mid-word cut is not theoretical. Every one of six ordinary wedding titles of 49-55 characters cut mid-word, byte-identical in all four room/width combinations: 'Photographs with both families by the lake\u2026 moved 7 days later.', 'Hair and make-up for the bridesmaids at the\u2026', 'Champagne and canapes on the west terrace b\u2026', 'Coach leaves the hotel for the church, plea\u2026', 'Ceremony music, readings and the exchange o\u2026', 'Welcome drinks for the early arrivals and t\u2026' \u2014 reproducing both seats' quoted strings exactly. 43 characters is not generous: fixture titles run 11-27, so the trim only ever fires on the owner's own typing, which is precisely the case round 11 shipped briefly() for. (b) The /[s,;:]+$/ class is the LETTER s and it does real harm in both directions. It never strips the whitespace it was written for: 'Musicians set up in the corner of the hall by the tall windows' slices to a trailing space and renders, visibly, as 'Musicians set up in the corner of the hall \u2026' with a floating gap before the ellipsis (screenshotted at 1440 on paper). And it silently eats a final s, changing the word: 'Room turnaround while the guests take drinks on the lawn outside' announces as '...take drink\u2026', and 'Photographs with both families by the lakeside steps' slices to '...by the lakes' and is served as '...by the lake\u2026'. A trim that turns 'drinks' into 'drink' and 'lakes' into 'lake' is worse than a plain mid-word cut \u2014 the stem left behind is a real word, so nothing signals that a letter was deleted. (c) The recovery defence fails on the delete path. On .b-undoText there is no data-clamp, no data-full, no title and no visually-hidden twin \u2014 the only attribute present is class. The comment at render-b.js:56 defends the trim with 'the full title is in the field two rows below', which holds for the stepper and hide paths but not for :1305: after 'Delete this moment' the editor and the row are both gone, and I asserted on the live DOM in all four combinations that the full string appears nowhere in document.body.innerText and in no attribute of any element on the page. The bar is role="status", so the mutated string is exactly what a screen-reader owner is told a moment was called, and it is the only remaining statement of what was removed. (d) It is not covered by the gates. interaction-check.mjs:432 and :439 do assert whole-word trimming and a full accessible twin, but both iterate document.querySelectorAll('[data-clamp]'), which .b-undoText is not; the long-title test at :3296 asserts only /moved 7 days later/ and never reads the half of the sentence that names the moment. This is the round notes' own 'a passing assertion that proves nothing' pattern, and it is the first entry under Typography in lessons.md ('Mid-word clamps... Trim to the last whole word, keep the full string in the accessible name and tooltip') creeping back inside round 11's own fix. Two corrections that do not save it: the second framing's aside that 'the bar measures 64px in all sixteen cases' is wrong at 390, where I measured 110px on both grounds \u2014 but that is the two-line wrap the round notes already describe, it is unchanged by the trim, and the finding is about the string, not the reserve.
sharpenedFix: Take the seat's fix, with the boundary tightened. render-b.js:59 \u2014 function briefly(record) { var name = nameOf(record); if (name.length <= 44) return name; var cut = name.slice(0, 43); var space = cut.lastIndexOf(' '); if (space >= 20) cut = cut.slice(0, space); return cut.replace(/[\\s,;:\\u2013\\u2014-]+$/, '') + '\u2026'; } \u2014 note the escaped \\s, which is the whole of defect (b), and the added dash so a title cut inside 'make-up' does not leave a hanging hyphen. The result is never longer than today's, so the 64px band at 1440, the two-line band at 390 and the label's 22-24px of air are all untouched; verify with the existing :3296 case. Then close the gate hole rather than writing a new assertion: in paintUndo(), when the first say[] part differs from nameOf(top.record), emit the name as span[data-clamp][data-full=<full title>][aria-hidden=true] followed by the sibling span[data-clamp-full="true"] holding the untrimmed title in the b-vh class \u2014 the exact shape .b-title already uses \u2014 so interaction-check.mjs:432 and :439 begin covering the one trim on the surface that is outside the product's own clamp engine. Confirm both assertions fail against the current code before fixing, or the coverage is not real.
